sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Areas
sections.content: Define a 2x2 determinant as the signed area of the parallelogram spanned by two column vectors. Explain that if the vectors are collinear, the area (determinant) is zero, implying no unique solution.
sections.example: Visualizing two vectors, v1=(2,0) and v2=(0,2), spanning a square area of 4 units.

sections.title: The Geometric Setup
sections.content: Represent the linear system Ax = b as a vector equation: x*(col1) + y*(col2) = b. Explain that we are looking for the scalar weights (x, y) that scale the column vectors to 'reach' the target vector b.
sections.example: A delivery drone (vector b) needs to reach a destination using two engine vectors (col1 and col2).

sections.title: Visualizing Cramer's Rule
sections.content: Show that scaling the first vector by x creates a new parallelogram with the second vector. The area of this 'new' parallelogram is (x * det(A)). By substitution, show that this new area is exactly the determinant of the matrix with the first column replaced by b.
sections.example: Replacing the 'x-axis engine' vector with the destination vector b to form a new, scaled shape.

sections.title: The Ratio Interpretation
sections.content: Synthesize the rule: x = det(Ax) / det(A). Explain this as the ratio of two areas: the area of the transformed parallelogram vs. the original unit-based parallelogram.
sections.example: If the original area is 2 and the 'replaced' area is 6, the drone must scale the first engine power by 3.

sections.title: Summary & Intuition
sections.content: Recap that Cramer's rule is simply measuring how much 'space' the target vector b occupies relative to the basis vectors provided by the matrix columns.
sections.example: A quick animation showing the 'morphing' of the parallelograms as the target b changes position.
